newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary still strong for NATO first round.
newsitem.headline: Hungary still strong for NATO first round.

text.p: Hungary remains a strong contender to join NATO in the first round of enlargement, along with Poland and the Czech Republic, Hungarian and U.S officials said on Tuesday.

The comments followed widespread play given by Hungarian media to a report attributed to the Belgian news agency Belga, quoting diplomatic sources, that Hungary's admission to the alliance could be deferred to a second round.
Foreign Ministry spokesman Gabor Szentivanyi insisted that Hungary had sound prospects of admission in the first wave. The Belgian report should be treated with "appropriate caution," he said.

U.S ambassador to Budapest Donald Blinken told Reuters: "Hungary has met as well as any of the other countries the so-called Perry standards...of readiness for NATO admission." He was referring to guidelines set down by former U.S. defence secretary William Perry.
Commenting on the press reports he said in an interview: "I find no basis at all for that in any of my conversations with people at home that would support such a theory."

Blinken said Hungary met NATO criteria in the areas of economic reform, parliamentary democracy, civilian control of the military and good relations with its neighbours but was having more difficulty with modernisation of its armed forces.

"There are not enough English-speaking officers yet to be fully comfortable in terms of dealing with serious NATO problems, but on the other hand they have made enormous progress in all of these areas," Blinken said.

He also said Hungary's performance in Partnership for Peace exercises, as well as Hungary's role in providing support facilities for NATO peacekeeping forces in Bosnia had all helped to boost the country's standing.

"I cannot see any reason, given Hungary's outstanding performance in the Partnership for Peace exercises, enormous support to NATO during the current Bosnian peacekeeping operation...and the progress Hungary has made in the last three or four years turning this economy around...to consider Hungary any differently from the Czech Republic or Poland," the ambassador said.
